questions.q: What is a review-board panelist often actually testing when they ask "why didn't you just do X" about an alternative design?
options: Whether the candidate actually considered the alternative and rejected it for a specific reason, rather than never having thought of it at all
Whether the candidate will immediately abandon their chosen design
Whether the candidate can recite the Salesforce terms of service
Whether the alternative is technically impossible to implement
questions.explain: A design that happens to be correct but was arrived at without considering alternatives is shakier under questioning than one that explicitly weighed options and chose deliberately.

questions.q: What does a rejected-alternatives table need to include for each alternative, according to this lesson?
options: Only the name of the alternative, nothing else
A list of every company that has ever used that alternative
The alternative, its main trade-off, and the specific, scenario-based reason it was rejected for this case
A cost estimate in dollars for implementing the alternative
questions.explain: Naming the alternative alone, or giving a one-line generic reason, doesn't convey the breadth of consideration a scenario-specific rejection reason does.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against "strawmanning" a rejected alternative?
options: Because strawmanning is a formally banned practice under Salesforce's certification program
Because misrepresenting the alternative's real strengths to make the chosen design look better reads as evasive to a panel, even when the final recommendation is correct
Because every alternative must always be chosen over the candidate's actual design
Because strawmanning only applies to technical risk, not business risk
questions.explain: A panel can tell the difference between a fairly considered and honestly rejected alternative and a caricatured one designed just to make the chosen answer look better by comparison.

questions.q: In the Carrow Equipment example, why was full data replication from SAP rejected as an alternative to Salesforce Connect for pricing and inventory?
options: Because data replication is not a real Salesforce capability
Because replication would have been cheaper but panels always prefer the more expensive option
Because SAP does not allow any form of data replication under its licensing
Because replication's inherent lag, however short, creates the exact stale-inventory risk the scenario specifically calls out as a real fulfillment problem
questions.explain: The rejection reason is tied specifically to this scenario's freshness requirement at the moment of ordering, not a general claim that replication is always wrong.

questions.q: What is the recommended response if a panel raises a genuinely new alternative the candidate hadn't considered before the question?
options: Insist the alternative was already fully considered and rejected, even if that isn't true
Refuse to answer the question since it wasn't prepared in advance
Engage with the alternative honestly in the moment and reason through how it compares to the proposed design
Immediately change the entire design to match the alternative without discussion
questions.explain: Panels generally respond better to honest, in-the-moment reasoning about a genuinely new alternative than to a candidate bluffing that it was already considered.
